title: States and typed events
goal: Describe legal transitions and handle typed events without implicit state changes.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–5: functions, STL, ownership, testing and multi-file builds.
Study the linked prerequisite topics below before this lesson.

sections.title: State determines permitted actions
paragraphs: Pause is legal only while running. Command P alone is insufficient: the result also depends on the current state. A state table makes that dependency testable.

Two independent flags called running and paused admit four combinations, including contradictory ones. enum class State names the meaningful states: idle, running, paused and done. For each event the machine checks its current state and selects a transition. An absent transition means rejection, not an arbitrary choice of a next state.

Draw the transition table: Start takes idle to running, Pause takes running to paused, Resume takes paused to running and Finish takes running to done. All other pairs are rejected. This is the laboratory specification. It supports discussing requirements before implementation: finishing while paused is deliberately forbidden here, although another product could permit it.

sections.title: An event type instead of a numeric convention
paragraphs: The empty structures Start, Pause, Resume and Finish represent distinct command types. using Event = std::variant<...> names a value that holds one of the listed alternatives. Unlike an untagged union, a variant tracks its active alternative. A single ordinary Event value cannot simultaneously contain both Start and Finish.

In the first example, Event event = Start{} constructs the Start alternative. Braces create an empty command object; it carries no user payload yet. A later Rename event could contain std::string title. Event types then associate each action with its required data and eliminate meaningless fields such as a title attached to Finish.

sections.title: visit selects Start
paragraphs: variant holds one event. decay_t removes const and reference from the parameter type; if constexpr selects the relevant branch at compile time.

sections.title: Reading std::visit
paragraphs: std::visit invokes a visitor with the alternative actually stored. The generic lambda receives const auto& item. decltype(item) describes that parameter’s type; std::decay_t removes reference and const qualifications for comparison. std::is_same_v<T, Start> is a compile-time boolean. It does not compare addresses or inspect the textual spelling of a type name.

if constexpr selects a suitable branch when the visitor is instantiated for a particular type. Each laboratory branch checks its state-transition pair and returns bool. All visitor paths return bool, making the result of visit consistent. Read the short example first, then trace apply with Pause while idle and explain why it returns false.

sections.title: From text to an event
paragraphs: The laboratory driver maps S, P, R and F into typed values. This translation belongs to the input adapter. The machine itself reads no cin and does not know whether a command came from a string, button or test. An unknown character increments rejected without changing state. An empty line is a valid empty trace.

The line is bounded to one hundred characters; extra non-whitespace data after it violates the protocol. A space inside the line is not ignored and counts as an unknown event. This precision prevents ambiguous tests. In a real GUI, a widget handler constructs the typed event; entering letters is not a substitute for the required graphical exercise.

sections.title: Invariants and rejection
paragraphs: A transition is committed only after checking the starting state. Rejection preserves state and increments rejected exactly once. done is terminal in this contract: the task cannot resume from it. A requirement to reopen work calls for a separate event and a revised transition table, rather than silently reusing Start.

SPF and SPRF differ by one Resume: the former remains paused with a rejection, while the latter reaches done. Paired tests expose overly permissive transitions. After adding a variant alternative, inspect the visitor: a general else can accidentally treat a new type as Finish. A stricter extension names Finish explicitly and statically rejects unhandled alternatives.

sections.title: Finish while idle
paragraphs: Calling finish need not finish the job: it checks the initial state first. Predict the call result and the separate s==idle check.

reveal.title: Reveal output and walkthrough
paragraphs: 0 1 confirms that rejection does not move the machine to done. List the legal source state for each of S,P,R,F in the lab.

tables.caption: What happens at each step
rows: 0 is rejection;1 confirms preservation of idle.

sections.title: Testing the machine
paragraphs: Visiting every state is insufficient: permitted and forbidden state-event pairs must be checked. Build a 4×4 matrix and mark the expected transitions. Choose short traces reaching each pair from initial idle. Separately test repeated Start, repeated Finish, an unknown character and an empty line. Each result includes both the final state and rejection count.

For transfer, design a document machine with draft, review and published states and a revision path. Establish domain rules before choosing types and tests. Do not copy the planner’s four states without analysis. The transferable skill is constructing a checkable transition contract used consistently by a text adapter, graphical interface and test driver.

sections.title: Laboratory contract: input to observation
paragraphs: Read one line of at most 100 characters. S maps idle→running, P running→paused, R paused→running, F running→done. Other pairs or characters count as one rejection without mutation. An empty line is valid; a missing line or extra data after it produces invalid.
Before running, trace the reference case. Write the state after each action and explain any expected rejection. Then compare the observed result with the labelled expectation below.

sections.title: Reading a working example
paragraphs: The variant constructs Start. visit receives Start and decay_t normalizes its type. if constexpr selects the start message. First identify data, ownership and the observable outcome. Then change exactly one initial condition and predict which observation changes. This connects syntax to a contract rather than memorizing finished source text.

The initial state is idle. finish is permitted only for running. false and true show rejection and retained idle. Compare the second example with the first: what new boundary is covered, and which test distinguishes the correct implementation from a superficially similar mistake? Retain both sources, predictions and actual observations so that the explanation can be reproduced.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Complete apply for four types. Keep character parsing outside: unknown X is one rejection, not a new event type.
Build a 4×4 table of legal pairs.

selfcheck.prompt: What does finish print for initial idle?
selfcheck.feedback: 0 1 confirms that rejection does not move the machine to done. List the legal source state for each of S,P,R,F in the lab.

selfcheck.prompt: What state and rejection count result from SPF starting at idle?
selfcheck.feedback: S enters running, P enters paused and F from paused is forbidden. Rejection preserves paused.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does the visitor apply decay_t to decltype(item) for const auto& item?
options: To compare the ordinary command type without const/reference.
To obtain the numeric code of an alternative.
To copy the active object to the heap.
selfcheck.feedback: is_same_v compares types. Without removing qualifications, const Start& differs from Start.

selfcheck.prompt: Reopen is added, but the visitor ends with a catch-all else previously meaning Finish. What is the risk?
options: Reopen may incorrectly follow the Finish branch.
std::visit automatically supplies the correct transition.
selfcheck.feedback: A catch-all else cannot distinguish new types. Explicit alternatives and completeness checking make extension controlled.

selfcheck.prompt: A space occurs inside the otherwise valid event line. What does the laboratory contract do?
options: Counts the unknown character as one rejection without a state change.
Ignores all whitespace within the line.
selfcheck.feedback: The protocol reads the whole line rather than skipping internal characters as formatted cin does. Space is not S/P/R/F.

selfcheck.prompt: Which test distinguishes terminal done from an incorrectly accepted repeated Start?
options: SFS, checking the state and one rejection.
selfcheck.feedback: SF reaches done and the following S must be rejected. The other traces never reach done and cannot test this prohibition.

selfcheck.prompt: Trace SPF. Why is F rejected after P? How can Reopen be added without the general else treating it as Finish?
selfcheck.feedback: idle→running→paused; F is legal only in running. Use an explicit Finish branch, then a separate Reopen rule and tests for all pairs.

practice.title: Laboratory: States and typed events
practice.task: Read one line of at most 100 characters. S maps idle→running, P running→paused, R paused→running, F running→done. Other pairs or characters count as one rejection without mutation. An empty line is valid; a missing line or extra data after it produces invalid.
criteria: SPF: paused rejected 1; empty line: idle rejected 0; X: idle rejected 1.
Add one valid scenario and one rejection of your own. Keep the sources, input/actions and observed outcome. Your explanation is reviewed separately from execution.
practice.hint: idle→running→paused; F is legal only in running. Use an explicit Finish branch, then a separate Reopen rule and tests for all pairs.

steps.why: The same event has different outcomes in different states.

steps.action: Complete the visitor and run SPRF.
steps.why: Assign state only in an accepted branch.

steps.action: Check SPF, an empty line and unknown X.
steps.why: An empty line differs from a missing line.
steps.expected: SPF: paused rejected 1; empty line: idle rejected 0; X: idle rejected 1.

terms.definition: States and transition rules driven by events.
A permitted state change for a specified event.
One of the types a variant can hold.
A callable applied to the active alternative.
A state without permitted outgoing transitions in the contract.
Conditional branch instantiation controlled by a compile-time constant.
A condition preserved at the boundaries of permitted model operations.
An agreed observation by which a client distinguishes contract satisfaction from a defect.
